title: What is connected TV? How CTV advertising works | Amazon Ads

facts.fact: Streaming TV (STV) is the digital distribution of video content across devices with an Internet connection, rather than a cable signal.
facts.quote: Streaming TV (STV) is the digital distribution of video content across devices with an Internet connection, rather than a cable signal.

facts.fact: Connected TV (CTV) refers to devices that are connected to the Internet and allow viewers to stream videos and music, and browse the web.
facts.quote: Connected TV (CTV) refers to devices that are connected to the Internet and allow viewers to stream videos and music, and browse the web.

facts.fact: Over-the-top (OTT) describes how content is distributed over the Internet without traditional satellite or cable providers, while CTV refers to the device used to view that content.
facts.quote: The difference between OTT and CTV is that the former refers to how the content is distributed over the Internet

facts.fact: Cost per completed view (CPCV) measures the price of each completed ad, and it is one of the marketing metrics used in CTV programmatic pricing alongside video completion rate (VCR).
facts.quote: based on marketing metrics such as video completion rate (VCR) and cost per completed view (CPCV). CPCV measures the price of each completed ad.

facts.fact: Amazon streaming TV ads are currently purchased programmatically, meaning ads are bought and sold digitally by an automated system.
facts.quote: Currently, Amazon streaming TV ads are purchased programmatically, meaning that the ads are bought and sold digitally by an automated system.

facts.fact: The video completion rate (VCR) of CTV ads tends to be very high because many streaming services do not allow ads to be skipped.
facts.quote: The VCR of CTV ads tend to be very high, since many streaming services do not allow ads to be skipped.
